chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"If you are Muhrim (in the state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah) in the al-Hill (the area outside the sacred boundary) and you kill game between yourself and the Haram (the sacred precincts), then upon you is its ransom. If you blind its eye or break its horn, you give charity. And whoever is in the Haram and throws (shoots) game in the al-Hill, upon him is the ransom." It was narrated.

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: al-Haram: the sacred precincts of Mecca
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: al-Hill: the area outside the sacred boundary of Mecca
key_terms.الْفِدَاءُ: al-Fida': the ransom/compensation for the killed game
key_terms.مُحِلًّا: Muhrim: one in the state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing game while in Ihram outside versus inside the Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the spatial distinction in fidyah liability, noting that killing game between the Hill and the Haram boundary incurs compensation, while wounding the animal specifically triggers a charitable donation. It further establishes that hunting within the Haram boundary while in Ihram requires fidyah, reflecting the stricter sanctity of the inner sacred zone. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the precise location of the 'Hill' relative to the 'Haram' during Hajj rituals.
